text: 300 years ago, one place on Earth made about a quarter of everything the whole world produced.
Not Britain.
Not China.
Not America.
Spices.
Cotton.
Steel.
Diamonds.
Ships came from the other side of the planet just to buy what India made.
Richest shop on the planet, and it was always open.
India was so rich, people had a name for it.
Soniki Chidia. The Golden Bird.
And when you're a Golden Bird, everyone wants to catch you.
Then, in less than 250 years,
that quarter shrank to about 4%.
Someone forgot to lock the shop. And here's the strange part.
This wasn't the first time. India has been rich,
and robbed and rebuilt again and again for 5,000 years. Over that time this land
was ruled by city builders nobody can name. An emperor who gave up war after one
terrible battle. Sultans, Mughals, a company, and finally its own people. A
company. I'll explain later. You will not believe it. Because if you look closely
India keeps living the same story. First, someone stitches the land together. Then it
shines, the richest place on earth. Then it shatters into pieces. Outsiders march in to
take it. And then, something strange happens. India absorbs them. The invaders end up eating
its food, speaking its languages, and building its monuments. Stitch. Shine. Shatter. Absorb.
again and again. So how did one land become the richest place in the world,
lose it all, and start climbing back? Hold on to something. Let's go back to the very beginning.
